name: Bernice
overview: Bernice, identified in Scripture as the daughter of King Agrippa, appears in the New Testament during the events recorded in Acts. She is mentioned alongside Agrippa when they visit Festus in Caesarea, indicating her presence in significant political and judicial moments (Acts 25:13). Later, she is noted sitting with King Agrippa and the governor as Paul makes his defense, highlighting her involvement in key interactions surrounding the early Christian witness (Acts 26:30). These references situate Bernice within the historical and cultural context of the early church, providing a glimpse into the worldly powers that intersected with the gospel message.
